note: Stop showing (REVEAL-6, REVEAL-22, X-3). TWO scopes: every copy of one document's disclosure, or every slot of the session. There is no slot scope: REVEAL-22 is `a Stop clears a slot only if it holds what the Stop names`, and a Stop that named an audience and nothing else could not honour it — tab A's retried Stop (REVEAL-16 retries with backoff) would clear whatever tab B had deliberately revealed into that slot meanwhile. Naming the document makes the rule hold by construction: a GM client always knows the document, because every slot's document id is in the GM's reveal picture, and a document has at most one live disclosure (owner decision O-3, amending ED-15's `at most one slot`), so what the Stop names is unambiguous however many copies that disclosure has - a Stop on the document clears every copy. A Stop carries NO epoch — it is never stale, never queued, never refused for state, and succeeds on an empty slot — so a stale number can never turn a narrowing into a refusal. There is no Retract in v1 (ED-16).

valid.name: stop showing this document, wherever it is live

invalid.name: a Stop carrying the reveal epoch
invalid.why: X-3, REVEAL-22: a narrowing is never stale and is never refused for state, so it carries no epoch to be stale against

invalid.name: Stop all carrying the reveal epoch
invalid.why: X-3: the same for the workspace indicator's Stop all, which is the panic button

invalid.name: a Stop that names a slot
invalid.why: REVEAL-22, REVEAL-16: a Stop clears a slot only if it holds what the Stop names, and a scope that named an audience alone could not honour that — a retried slot Stop would kill a later, deliberate reveal into the same slot, so the scope does not exist

invalid.name: Stop all naming an audience
invalid.why: Stop all clears every slot of the session, and no Stop names an audience at all: a Stop names a document, or all

invalid.name: a document scope naming an audience as well
invalid.why: one scope per Stop: a document Stop clears every copy of that document's disclosure (REVEAL-7, O-3), and an audience beside it would be a second rule with no way to tell which applied

invalid.name: a scope this contract does not define
invalid.why: closed vocabulary: a Retract is the assistant's Phase 4, not a v1 scope (ED-16)

invalid.name: a Stop with no command id
invalid.why: a Stop is retried until acknowledged (REVEAL-16), so it must be recognisable as the same command
